issues.description: Three patches stuffed into one commit
issues.detail: The crash-log buffering fix is the real change. Reordering _queue_msg in worker.py, disabling pytest-xdist (-n auto), removing test_plugin_google_stt.py from the suite, and adding pythonpath to pyproject are all unrelated. When the log buffering regresses in six months, bisect lands on a commit that also touched the worker accept flow. Split it: one patch per intent.

issues.description: OTLP handler lookup by isinstance is fragile coupling
issues.detail: _flush_early_log_buffer and _shutdown_telemetry both walk root.handlers looking for opentelemetry.sdk._logs.LoggingHandler instances. If anyone else attaches a LoggingHandler, or the SDK refactors the class, this silently breaks. The module that *installs* the handler should hand back a reference; don't introspect global state to find what you just added.

_BufferingHandler.buffer is a plain list with no cap. If a job hangs for a long time before crashing or session.start() never lands, this grows until the process dies. A crash-log buffer that itself causes the crash is bad taste. Cap it (ring buffer, max records, or max bytes) and log when truncation happens.

Dropping `-n auto` serializes the whole unit-test suite. That's a real wall-clock regression for every contributor and CI run. If a specific test is flaky under xdist, fix or mark that test; don't punish the suite. And test_plugin_google_stt.py is silently removed with no commit message explanation — why?

issues.description: init_recording side-effect on the early-return path is surprising
issues.detail: init_recording now calls _stop_log_buffering() before returning when already initialized or non-cloud. That's a mutation hidden behind a guard that reads like a no-op. Either pull the stop call out above the guard with a comment, or rename so the side effect is visible. Future readers will miss it.

If init_recording raises in the crash path, the except logs and calls _stop_log_buffering, but the buffered records are dropped on the floor with no indication to the operator that crash logs were lost. At minimum, count and log how many records were discarded so someone debugging an outage knows the upload didn't happen.

review.summary: The core change — buffer logs early, flush through OTLP when recording initializes, force shutdown on crash so cleanup can flush — is the right shape and solves a real operator pain. But this is THREE-PATCHES masquerading as one: the crash-log fix is tangled with an unexplained worker.py reorder, pytest-xdist disablement, a silently removed test file, and a pyproject change. The buffer is unbounded and the OTLP handler is found by isinstance-walking root.handlers — both are fragile. NEEDS-WORK: split the commit, bound the buffer, return the OTLP handler from the setup function instead of fishing for it, and justify or revert the makefile changes.
